svg.aria-label: What to do if you suspect a child marriage is being arranged. First, ask whether the child is in immediate danger. If yes, call the Uganda Child Helpline on 116, free on any network, or go to the nearest police Child and Family Protection Unit now. If no, do not confront the family publicly and do not post anything online. Speak with the child privately if it is safe to do so and ask what she wants. Contact a formal route: Sauti 116, the district probation and social welfare officer, the police Child and Family Protection Unit, or a legal aid provider. Write down what you know and keep it somewhere private. Then stay alongside her, because a referral nobody follows up is not protection.
svg.text: If you think a child marriage is being arranged
General guidance, not legal advice. When in doubt, call 116 and ask.
Is she in immediate danger?
YES: act now
Call the Uganda Child Helpline on 116
free on any network, 24 hours, or go
to the nearest police Child and Family
Protection Unit.
NO: still act, carefully
There is time to do this properly.
Work through the steps below rather
than raising it with the family first.
Do not confront, do not post
Naming her publicly or online can increase the danger and end her cooperation.
Speak with her privately, if it is safe
Ask what she wants to happen. Her view should shape what you do next.
Use a formal route
Sauti 116 · district probation and social welfare officer · police CFPU · legal aid.
Write down what you know, keep it private
Dates, names, what was said. Store it where the family cannot find it.
Never: name a child on social media · promise secrecy you cannot keep · investigate it yourself.
Treasured Vessels Girls’ Centre · treasuredvesselsuganda.org
